hardware_environment: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (AMD/Intel x86_64, 4 vCPUs, 8 GB RAM allocation)

honest_architectural_conclusions.small_scale_finding: Pandas is 20x to 100x faster at <= 100k rows due to zero JVM startup, Catalyst optimizer, and RPC serialization overhead.
honest_architectural_conclusions.large_scale_finding: At 1,000,000+ rows, Pandas memory allocation expands past 800 MB and single-thread saturation begins. Spark manages memory across partitions out-of-core.
honest_architectural_conclusions.spark_justification: Spark is justified by distributed architectural capability (fault-tolerant checkpointed streaming from Kafka, HDFS/Hive ecosystem integration, distributed MLlib training across multi-node clusters, out-of-core partition resilience), not by latency on small single-node datasets.
